class.name: GazeModifier3D
class.brief_description: Turns the eyes, head, neck and upper back together to look at a target, with human gaze dynamics.
class.description: A look at a target shared over a chain of bones, on top of whatever the animation does. It follows the head-eye coordination model of Andrist, Pejsa, Mutlu and Gleicher ("A Head-Eye Coordination Model for Animating Gaze Shifts of Virtual Characters", 2012) and the torso alignment of Pejsa et al. (2015): the eyes lead and carry what fits in their range, the head follows [member head_latency] later and carries the rest up to [member head_yaw_limit], and the upper back joins only for the part of the turn past [member spine_start_angle]. Each part moves with second-order dynamics (see [SecondOrderDynamics]), so gaze shifts start quickly, overshoot slightly and settle, and bigger shifts move faster. A faint quasi-periodic drift keeps a held look alive. Angles are measured in the character's frame: [member reference_node]'s, whose +Z is forward and +Y up (the skeleton's own if it is empty), so rigs whose armature is turned under the character's node aim correctly. Each bone's forward is taken from the rest pose. Rigs without eye bones are fine: the head then carries the whole look from a point [member eye_offset] from the head bone. Everything advances with the modifier's delta only, so a stopped clock holds the pose exactly (path-traced stills accumulate cleanly). Use [method reset] after a cut. Unlike [LookAtModifier3D], which aims one bone with a tween, this distributes the look over the chain and moves it with springs.

method.name: angles_to
method.description: The yaw (left positive) and pitch (down positive) in radians of [param global_position] from the character's eyes, in the character's frame, as the skeleton's pose is now.

method.name: get_head_angles
method.description: Where the head ended up facing on the last modification: yaw (left positive) and pitch (down positive) in radians, in the character's frame.

method.name: get_look_weight
method.description: How much of the look is applied, [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]: it fades in when a target is looked at and out when there is none or it is beyond [member ignore_angle].

method.name: get_target_angles
method.description: The angles of the target on the last modification, clamped to the limits: yaw and pitch in radians.

method.name: reset
method.description: Snaps the gaze to the current target on the next modification, with no motion from the previous one. Call it after a camera cut or a teleport.

members.member: The amplitude of the slow drift added to the head's aim, so a held look is never perfectly still. [code]0.0[/code] turns it off.
The drift's base frequency in hertz.
Varies the drift's phase, so characters do not drift in step.
The eyes' damping ratio.
How far the eyes turn down from the head's facing.
How fast the eyes respond, in hertz. Eyes are fast (saccades).
Where the eyes are from the head bone, in metres in the character's frame, for rigs without eye bones.
The eyes' initial response (see [member SecondOrderDynamics.response]).
How far the eyes turn up from the head's facing.
How far the eyes turn left or right from the head's facing.
How fast the look fades in and out, in hertz.
The head bone. Required.
The head's damping ratio: below [code]1.0[/code] the head overshoots slightly and settles.
How far the head (with the neck) tips down.
How fast the head responds, in hertz.
How long after the eyes the head starts to follow, in seconds.
The head's initial response; a small negative value gives a slight anticipation.
How far the head (with the neck) tips up.
How far the head (with the neck) turns left or right before the upper back has to help.
A target further round than this (behind the character) is not looked for; the look fades out.
The left eye bone, optional. With both eyes set, each also converges on a near target.
The neck bone, optional. It takes [member neck_share] of the head's turn.
The neck's share of the head's turn; the head bone takes the rest.
The character's node: its +Z is the character's forward and +Y its up. Empty uses the skeleton's frame.
The right eye bone, optional.
The upper back's bones, from the lowest, that share the part of the turn past [member spine_start_angle]. Optional.
Each spine bone's share of the back's turn; empty or short means equal shares.
How far round the look goes before the upper back starts to turn with it.
The most the upper back turns.
What the character looks at.
The node looked at, when [member target_mode] is [constant TARGET_MODE_NODE].
The global position looked at, when [member target_mode] is [constant TARGET_MODE_POSITION].

constants.constant: Looks at nothing: the look fades out to the animation's own head.
